question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit outbound recipient allowlist for Slack message sends now, and should that policy be Slack-specific channel config or part of a shared human-chat outbound target policy?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but adding `allowTo`/`dmAllowTo` changes public config and outbound authorization semantics under the documented trusted-operator model, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary by itself.

options.title: Add explicit outbound target policy
options.body: Add a documented allowTo-style recipient policy with schema, docs, tests, and enforcement before Slack delivery while keeping `allowFrom` inbound-only.

options.title: Fold into broader guardrails
options.body: Track Slack recipient allowlisting as one acceptance case under the broader outbound guardrails work at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87870.

options.title: Decline core allowTo for now
options.body: Keep the trusted-operator model unchanged and document that `dmPolicy` and `allowFrom` do not constrain explicit operator sends.

recommendation.title: Add explicit outbound target policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented allowTo-style recipient policy with schema, docs, tests, and enforcement before Slack delivery while keeping `allowFrom` inbound-only.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the closest prior message policy work and is already the strongest history signal for the config/security boundary decision.
